new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (57 pp. QUOTE: p. 5 (PDF p. 5), sec. 2 'Background information', reads exactly: 'A note on pronunciation: both Awyu and Yaqay have a predominance of stress on the final syllable of a word. Thus place names are pronounced Ketá, Kotúp, Nohón, Bagarám, Wanggaté, Kogó, and Rayám, among others. Also, the "q" in Yaqay and the "gh" in Aghu represent voiced velar fricatives.' -- verbatim as reported. A a full-text search for stress/accent the report finds no other stress statement (only Appendix F rule 9 'accents.. are ignored'). READING: agree fixed: final syllable as the only available reading of the explicit statement, with the other reader's low confidence fully justified: it is a hedged s…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls predominantly on the word-final syllable (an impressionistic tendency statement by SIL surveyors, illustrated with village names Ketá, Nohón, Bagarám from the Central Awyu area; not a phonological analysis).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said (Appendix D wordlists occasionally carry a secondary-stress mark, e.g. Busiri ˌxɑbiˈroŋ 'hair', without comment).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; 'predominance' implies non-final cases exist. The report's own Appendix D IPA wordlists (Busiri, Ketah, Nohon, Taim) mark many penultimate stresses -- by a rough script tally only the Taim list is clearly final-dominant.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms / place names; 'Awyu' here = the Wildeman River Awyu villages surveyed (Keta, Nohon, Taim, Bagaram I, Busiri), i.e. the former Awyu Nohon [AWJ] area renamed Central Awyu [awu] (fn. 3 p. 4; Table 15 p. 28; Lebold et al. 2013 App. A). The sentence lumps Awyu with Yaqay and is a survey-report aside, not a phonology section.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted sentence speaks of 'Awyu' generically (and lumps it with Yaqay), but the Awyu villages of the Wildeman River survey it introduces -- Keta, Nohon, Taim, Bagaram I (and Busiri) -- are the former 'Awyu Nohon [AWJ]' area that SIL renamed Central Awyu [awu] = cent2118 (K&L 2010 fn. 3; Lebold et al. 2013 App. A p. 25); Glottolog/lexibank file the four K&L wordlists (Busiri, Ketah, Nohon, Taim) under cent2118, though K&L themselves suggest Busiri may be Asue Awyu [psa]. Drabbe's 1947/1950 'Pisa' (informants originally from the Wildeman) is filed by Glottolog under asue1235, not cent2118. Related first-hand final-stress statements exist only for the sister language Aghu (aghu1255: Drabbe 1957 / van den Heuvel 2016 / de Vries 2020 'weak accent on the last syllable').

sources.note: Sec. 2, p. 5: 'both Awyu and Yaqay have a predominance of stress on the final syllable of a word', illustrated with place names (Ketá, Nohón, Bagarám = Central Awyu villages). Appendix D (pp. 40-53) gives 239-item IPA wordlists for Busiri, Ketah, Nohon, Taim with primary-stress marks but no placement statement; my rough script tally of those marks is final-dominant only for Taim (107 final vs 29 penult), mixed for Nohon (55/43) and penult-leaning for Ketah (37/59) and Busiri (44/62).
